text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Bosnia's new council of ministers due to meet in Sarajevo's National Museum. Discussions will focus on 1997 budget, creation of new central bank and cooperation between Serb republic and Moslem-Croat federation to reopen state enterprises such as railways.
- Process of privatisation is going very slowly and reflects ambiguous economic and political situation in ruling structures in Bosnia, says Oslobodjenje commentary.

- Islamic religious celebration Ramadan begins today. Haris Silajdzic, co-chairman of Bosnian council of ministers, and commander of Bosnian army, General Rasim Delic, send greetings to Bosnian Moslems.

- Survey conducted by Dnevni Avaz says 31 percent of Bosnians think that decision on status of disputed town of Brcko will be made by February 14 deadline. But a majority of 51 percent expect decision to be postponed again.
- Workers who were obliged to quit their posts due to "state of war" still have their jobs following lifting of decree, says minister for social affairs and refugees.

- End of Bosnian war has cleared way for tax collection on fuel, newspaper says. All relief organisations currently in Bosnia have agreed to pay taxes, except NATO-led force which has special arrangement with authorities and main U.N. relief agency which has yet to reach an agreement with government.
- International reconstruction efforts revive gas network in heavily damaged Sarajevo suburbs of Nedzarici and Sokolje.
